status_summary: The pipeline has come mainly through a statute, a presidential memorandum and band-specific agency work rather than a single strategy document. Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) restored the FCC's general auction authority through 2034 and, per a Congressional Research Service report of 2026-02-25, requires the FCC to auction at least 300 MHz (including at least 100 MHz in the Upper C-band within two years, by about 2027-07-04) and NTIA to identify 500 MHz of federal spectrum between 1.3 and 10.5 GHz for reallocation, with at least 200 MHz of it identified within two years and the FCC to auction at least 200 MHz of that within four years and the rest within eight (the report's text and table are not fully consistent on these milestones). CRS also describes a presidential memorandum of 2025-12-19 (Winning the 6G Race) that directed NTIA to begin studies at once and to report on relocating the 7.125 to 7.4 GHz band by 2026-12-19. NTIA said on 2026-07-31 that it had cleared the last of four simultaneous repurposing studies, covering the 1.6 GHz, 2.7 GHz, 4.4 GHz and lower 7 GHz bands. On the FCC side, a final Upper C-band rule (adopted 2026-07-22, published 2026-07-31, effective 2026-09-29) makes 160 MHz in 3.98 to 4.14 GHz available for terrestrial wireless use with incumbent relocation and aircraft altimeter rebates, and a notice published 2026-08-03 proposes starting Auction 115 on 2027-04-27. No auction under the new pipeline has been held, and the CRS report did not indicate that NTIA had yet identified any of the 500 MHz. No single national spectrum strategy document was found.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 restores the FCC's general auction authority through 2034 and sets a spectrum pipeline: FCC auctions of at least 300 MHz (including at least 100 MHz at 3.98 to 4.2 GHz within two years) and NTIA identification of 500 MHz of federal spectrum between 1.3 and 10.5 GHz (per CRS).
FCC proposed rule on the Upper C-band (3.98 to 4.2 GHz) offers options of 100 to 180 MHz for terrestrial wireless use.
A presidential memorandum (Winning the 6G Race, as described by CRS) directs NTIA to begin spectrum studies immediately and to submit 7.125 to 7.4 GHz relocation results by 2026-12-19.

FCC final rule (adopted 2026-07-22, effective 2026-09-29) makes 160 MHz at 3.98 to 4.14 GHz available for terrestrial wireless use through competitive bidding, with a 20 MHz guard band, incumbent relocation and aircraft altimeter rebates.

NTIA announces it has cleared plans to study the 4.4 GHz band, so studies of the 1.6 GHz, 2.7 GHz, 4.4 GHz and 7 GHz bands are all under way; the congressional mandate is to identify 500 MHz within five years as NTIA describes it.
FCC notice schedules Upper C-band Auction 115 (3,248 licenses in 3.98 to 4.14 GHz) to start 2027-04-27 and seeks comment on bidding procedures.

uncertainties: The December 2025 presidential memorandum is described only through the CRS report and NTIA's release (which does not name the year); no text was found, and a Federal Register search for 6G in presidential documents returned none. A search for presidential documents on a national spectrum strategy also returned none (federalregister.gov) The CRS report's text and table disagree on the FCC auction schedule for NTIA-identified spectrum, and it predates the July 2026 actions; NTIA's 2026-07-31 release describes the identification deadline as five years while CRS lists two-year and four-year milestones. The Public Law 119-21 signing date of 2025-07-04 is inferred from the statutory two-year deadline of July 4, 2027 in the FCC rule. The spectrum.gov page refers to the law by another name (Working Families Tax Cut Act). Whether Auction 113 (AWS-3) has been held was not checked. Whether the White House and Congress built a general federal and commercial coordination process beyond the NTIA and FCC consultation in the statute was not confirmed.
